chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade sleeping on a roof that is not enclosed by a wall.

key_terms.سَطْحٍ: Roof or flat top of a building
key_terms.مُحَجَّرٍ: Enclosed or walled off (with a boundary wall)
key_terms.يُبَاتَ: To spend the night / to sleep

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sleeping on an open roof?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a specific legal ruling (hukm) regarding architectural safety, prohibiting sleeping on rooftops that lack a protective boundary wall (hijar) to prevent accidental falls. In Shia jurisprudence, this is often cited as a foundational example of 'la darar wa la dirar' (no harm) applied to domestic architecture, emphasizing the preservation of life (hifz al-nafs) through preventive measures. The narration highlights the Prophet's attention to practical details of daily life, linking physical safety to religious observance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade to sleep upon the roof other than in an enclosure (boundary wall)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn af-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, prohibited sleeping on the flat roof without a safety fencing wall around it.’”
